question: In a left CN VI (abducens) palsy, the esotropia is GREATEST when the patient looks to the LEFT (towards the affected side), and the left eye fails to abduct past the midline.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. CN VI palsy paralyses the ipsilateral lateral rectus. Attempting to look towards the affected side maximally recruits the paralysed muscle, producing the largest angle of esotropia. Always check if deviation increases on gaze toward the affected side.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — TRUE. The left lateral rectus is paralysed, so maximum separation of the visual axes (greatest esotropia) occurs when the patient attempts to look left. This gaze-dependent increase in angle is the hallmark of incomitant strabismus.
